sources.quote: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada counts roughly 41,300 employer establishments in computer systems design and related services, plus about 74,900 non-employer locations
sources.publisher: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
sources.title: Computer systems design and related services - 5415 - Businesses - Canadian Industry Statistics - Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
sources.evidence: For this industry, 74,857 establishments are non-employers or indeterminate and 41,303 have one or more employees. Source: Statistics Canada, special tabulation, unpublished data, unclassified excluded, 2025.

sources.quote: Google requires in-person customer contact during stated hours, so online-only firms are ineligible for a Business Profile
sources.title: Business eligibility and ownership guidelines - Google Business Profile Help
sources.evidence: To qualify for a Business Profile, a business must make in-person contact with customers during its stated hours. If your online-only business doesn't have a physical location that your customers can visit nor do you visit customers in-person, your business isn't eligible.

sources.quote: up to 20 service areas, with the total inside roughly two hours of driving from base
sources.title: Manage your service areas for service-area & hybrid businesses - Google Business Profile Help
sources.evidence: You can have up to 20 service areas. The boundaries of your overall area shouldn't be more than about 2 hours of driving time from where your business is based. You can't set your service area as a radius distance around your business.

sources.quote: Statistics Canada's cyber security and cybercrime survey found 16 percent of Canadian businesses were affected by an incident in 2023
sources.title: The Daily — Impact of cybercrime on Canadian businesses, 2023
sources.evidence: In 2023, about 1 in 6 (16%) Canadian businesses were impacted by cyber security incidents. Data for the 2023 Canadian Survey of Cyber Security and Cybercrime were collected from January to March 2024, with respondents asked to only report activities that occurred in 2023.

sources.quote: Ontario's Enhancing Digital Security and Trust Act, enacted through Bill 194 and largely in force since January 2025
sources.title: Enhancing Digital Security and Trust Act | Government of Ontario
sources.evidence: Bill 194, Strengthening Cyber Security and Building Trust in the Public Sector Act, 2024, received Royal Assent on November 25, 2024, introducing the Enhancing Digital Security and Trust Act, 2024. The Enhancing Digital Security and Trust Act, 2024 came into effect on January 29, 2025. It enables the government to set regulation requirements and directives governing cyber security in public sector organizations, with regulations requiring them to develop and implement cyber security programs.

sources.quote: The provision this industry forgets covers installing computer programs on someone else's device
sources.title: Canada's Anti-Spam Legislation Requirements for Installing Computer Programs | CRTC
sources.evidence: CASL requires you to obtain consent from the owner or another authorized user of the computer or device prior to the installation of a computer program. When installing a computer program on another person's computer system in the course of a commercial activity, you must obtain the express consent from the owner or authorized user, and when requesting this consent, you must clearly and simply describe the function and purpose of the program.

sources.quote: The Competition Act requires performance claims to rest on adequate and proper testing done before the claim is made, and the burden sits with the advertiser
sources.title: Performance claims not based on an adequate and proper test
sources.evidence: Under paragraph 74.01(1)(b) of the Competition Act, you cannot make a claim about a product's performance, its effectiveness, or its length of life, unless you can prove that the claim is based on an adequate and proper test. In addition, the test must have been done before the claim is made.

sources.quote: Since 20 June 2025, competitors and clients can seek leave from the Competition Tribunal to bring deceptive-marketing applications directly
sources.title: Private access to the Competition Tribunal
sources.evidence: Private access rights have been extended to cases involving deceptive marketing practices, and these changes come into force on June 20, 2025. Starting June 20, 2025, people can directly apply for permission to file an application against businesses under the deceptive marketing practices provisions of the Act. If you want to apply, you must first ask the Competition Tribunal for leave (permission).

sources.quote: breaches creating a real risk of significant harm must be reported to the Privacy Commissioner and notified to affected individuals, with records of all breaches kept 24 months regardless
sources.publisher: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
sources.title: What you need to know about mandatory reporting of breaches of security safeguards - Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
sources.evidence: Organizations subject to PIPEDA are required to report to the Privacy Commissioner of Canada breaches of security safeguards involving personal information that pose a real risk of significant harm to individuals and notify affected individuals about those breaches. Organizations must maintain a record of every breach of security safeguards for 24 months after the day on which the organization determines that the breach has occurred, regardless of whether they present a real risk of significant harm.

sources.quote: legacy Silver and Gold benefits stopped being sold in January 2025
sources.title: Silver or Gold Membership - Partner Center | Microsoft Learn
sources.evidence: Legacy silver/gold competencies were retired on September 30, 2022 and replaced with Solutions Partner designations. Starting January 22, 2025, Microsoft will no longer sell legacy silver/gold benefits, with the last day to purchase or renew these offerings being January 21, 2025.

sources.quote: Windows 10 support ended on 14 October 2025, and Microsoft sells Extended Security Updates to commercial customers for up to three years
sources.title: Extended Security Updates (ESU) program for Windows 10 | Microsoft Learn
sources.evidence: Individuals or organizations who elect to continue using Windows 10 after support ends on October 14, 2025, will have the option of enrolling their PCs into a paid ESU subscription. Enrolled PCs belonging to a commercial or educational organization can receive security updates for a maximum of three years after end of support for Windows 10.
